title: Car pulls to one side
h1: Why does my car pull to one side?
metaDesc: Car pulling left or right? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's tire pressure, alignment, a sticking brake or worn parts, and how urgent it is.
synonyms: have to hold steering wheel to go straight
intro: A car that pulls to one side usually has a tire, alignment or brake problem on one side that the other side doesn't. A slow drift that's been there for months is a different story from a pull that started suddenly. Answer the questions below to find the likely cause and how soon to deal with it.
safety: If the pull started suddenly with a bang, a thump or a corner sitting lower, pull over and don't drive it further.
If you smell burning or see smoke from a wheel, pull over, stop and let it cool. Don't touch the wheel.
If you have to fight the steering wheel to stay in your lane, slow down and get off the road safely.

opts.a: It started suddenly and pulls hard
All the time, even on a flat road
Only on some roads, usually drifting toward the curb or road edge

q_sudden.q: Did you notice any of these when it started?

opts.a: A tire looks flat or very low
A bang or clunk, or one corner now sits lower than the others
A burning smell, or one wheel is much hotter than the others
It started after hitting a pothole or curb
None of these / I'm not sure

q_pressure.q: Check all four tire pressures when the tires are cold and compare them with the sticker in the driver's door jamb. What did you find?
q_pressure.help: Use the number on the door jamb sticker, not the maximum printed on the tire. "Cold" means the car has been parked for a few hours or driven less than a mile.

opts.a: One tire is noticeably lower than the others
I can't check right now / I'm not sure
It started after new tires or a tire rotation
It started after hitting a pothole or curb, or after an accident
The steering also feels loose, or there's clunking over bumps
One wheel feels much hotter than the others after a drive
None of these / I'm not sure

result.title: A flat or very low tire is pulling the car
result.now: Pull over somewhere safe and stop. Put on the spare or call roadside assistance.
if: If the tire is only somewhat low and you're near a safe spot, you can add air there, then have it checked for a leak.
If the spare is a small temporary one, follow the speed and distance limits printed on it.
result.why: A tire that's lost a lot of air drags on that side and pulls the car toward it. Driving on it can destroy the tire, damage the wheel and make the car harder to control.

causes.name: Puncture from a nail or screw
causes.clues: The tire lost air over hours or days.

causes.name: Damage from a pothole or curb
causes.clues: Sudden air loss right after an impact, or a bulge on the sidewall.

causes.name: Leaking valve stem or wheel rim
causes.clues: Slow, repeated air loss with no visible puncture.

you: Look for a nail, screw or cut in the tread.
Check the spare's pressure before you rely on it.
shop: Tire leak inspection and repair or replacement

result.title: A suspension or steering part may have broken
result.now: Pull over safely and stop. Have the car towed or call a mobile mechanic to look at it where it is.
if: If a tire is touching the body or a broken spring is pressing against it, don't move the car at all.
If the steering wheel is now badly off-center, that's another sign something is bent or broken.
result.why: A sudden hard pull with a bang, or a corner that sits low, points to a broken coil spring, a broken or bent control arm, or a failed ball joint. These parts hold the wheel in place, so a failure can affect steering and braking.

causes.name: Broken coil spring
causes.clues: One corner sits lower, and there was a bang or clunk over a bump.

causes.name: Bent or broken control arm or tie rod
causes.clues: A hard impact, and the wheel looks tilted or the steering is off-center.

causes.name: Failed ball joint
causes.clues: Clunking that got worse before this happened.

you: From a safe spot, look at whether one corner sits lower or a wheel looks tilted.
shop: Suspension and steering inspection on a lift
Spring, control arm and ball joint check

result.title: A brake is probably sticking on that side
result.now: Park and let the brakes cool. Get the brakes checked within a day or two, and keep any driving short and gentle until then.
if: If you see smoke, or the burning smell comes back quickly, don't drive it. Have it towed.
If the brake pedal feels soft or goes lower than usual, stop driving and have it towed.
result.why: When a brake caliper or hose doesn't release fully, that wheel keeps braking lightly. The car pulls toward that side, the wheel gets very hot, and the brakes can overheat and stop working as well as they should.

causes.name: Sticking brake caliper
causes.clues: One wheel is much hotter than the others, with a burning smell or extra brake dust on that wheel.

causes.name: Collapsed brake hose
causes.clues: The pull comes and goes, and the brake on that side seems to stay on after you release the pedal.

causes.name: Parking brake not fully releasing
causes.clues: It's the rear wheel that's hot, and the parking brake has been sticky.

you: After a short drive, carefully hold your hand near (not on) each wheel to compare heat.
Make sure the parking brake is fully released.
shop: Brake caliper and slide pin inspection
Check each wheel spins freely on a lift

result.title: A hit to a wheel may have knocked the alignment out or bent a part
result.now: Have the alignment and front suspension inspected within the next few days. Drive gently until then.
if: If the pull gets stronger, the steering wheel is badly off-center, or you hear clunking, stop driving and have it towed.
If a tire has a bulge or a wheel is dented, don't drive on it. Put on the spare.
result.why: A pothole, curb or accident can shift the alignment or bend a tie rod, control arm or wheel. Even a small bend can make the car pull and wear the tires quickly. Bent parts need replacing, not just an alignment.

causes.name: Alignment knocked out
causes.clues: The steering wheel is now off-center when driving straight.

causes.name: Bent tie rod or control arm
causes.clues: The alignment can't be set back to normal, or one wheel looks tilted.

causes.name: Damaged tire or bent wheel
causes.clues: A bulge, a dent in the rim, or a new vibration.

you: Check the tire and wheel on the side that was hit.
Note whether the steering wheel is centered when driving straight.
shop: Steering and suspension parts inspection for bends

result.title: A pull when braking usually means one brake is working harder than the other
result.now: Have the brakes inspected within the next few days.
if: If the pedal feels soft or sinks, or you see fluid near a wheel, stop driving and have it towed.
If the pull is strong enough to move you out of your lane, don't drive it until it's fixed.
result.why: When the brakes on one side grip harder or the other side grips less, the car turns toward the stronger side every time you stop. It can come from a sticking caliper, contaminated pads or a worn suspension part that shifts under braking.

causes.name: Sticking or seized brake caliper
causes.clues: One wheel is hotter, or that wheel has more brake dust.

causes.name: Brake pads contaminated with oil or brake fluid
causes.clues: A wet or oily look on the inside of one wheel.

causes.name: Worn control arm bushings
causes.clues: A clunk when you first brake, and the pull comes on suddenly.

you: Look for wet spots on the inside of each wheel.
Compare how hot each wheel feels (without touching) after driving.

result.title: Pulling only under acceleration points to the drivetrain or its mounts
result.now: Book an inspection of the engine mounts, axles and front suspension bushings.
if: If you hear clunking or clicking when accelerating, get it checked within a few days.
If the car is a powerful front-wheel-drive model and the pull is mild under hard acceleration only, some of this can be normal.
result.why: On front-wheel-drive cars, power going to the front wheels can tug the steering to one side, especially under hard acceleration. Worn mounts or bushings let parts shift under load and make this much stronger.

causes.name: Worn engine or transmission mounts
causes.clues: A jolt or clunk when you start accelerating.

causes.name: Worn control arm bushings
causes.clues: Clunks over bumps and a pull that changes between accelerating and braking.

causes.name: Mismatched tires on the front
causes.clues: Different brands, sizes or wear on the two front tires.

you: Check that both front tires are the same brand and size, with similar wear.

result.title: This may be the slope of the road, not the car
result.now: Test on a flat, empty parking lot. Drive straight slowly and loosen your grip on the wheel for a moment. If the car stays straight, the road slope is the likely cause.
if: If the car drifts on a flat lot too, check the tire pressures and book an alignment check.
If the steering wheel is off-center when driving straight, have the alignment checked.
result.why: Most roads are built slightly higher in the middle so rain drains off. That slope gently pushes cars toward the edge. A mild drift that only happens on some roads is often just that.

causes.name: Road crown (slope)
causes.clues: The drift goes away on flat roads and changes when you change lanes.

causes.name: Slightly low tire
causes.clues: One tire is a few PSI lower than the others.

causes.name: Alignment slightly off
causes.clues: The drift is there on flat roads too, or the tires wear on one edge.

you: Test on a flat parking lot.

result.title: A low tire is the most likely reason it's pulling
result.now: Inflate all four tires to the pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker, then see if the pull goes away.
if: If the same tire is low again within a few days, have it checked for a leak.
If the pressures are right and it still pulls, book an alignment check.
result.why: A tire with less air has more drag and a slightly smaller rolling size, so the car pulls toward that side. It's the simplest cause to rule out and the cheapest to fix.

causes.name: Low tire pressure on one side
causes.clues: One tire reads lower than the others, or the TPMS light is on.

causes.name: Slow leak
causes.clues: The same tire keeps losing air.

causes.name: Alignment off as well
causes.clues: The pull stays after the pressures are correct.

you: Inflate the tires and test drive on a flat road.
Recheck the low tire after a day or two.

result.title: A new or rotated tire may be causing the pull
result.now: Go back to the tire shop and ask them to swap the two front tires side to side and check the alignment.
if: If the pull switches to the other side after the swap, one tire is the cause and should be replaced.
If the pull stays the same after the swap, the alignment is the more likely problem.
result.why: Some tires are built slightly unevenly inside, which makes them roll toward one side. This is called tire pull or radial pull. It shows up right after tires are installed or moved, and swapping the front tires is a simple way to prove it.

causes.name: Tire with built-in pull (radial pull)
causes.clues: The pull started right after new tires or a rotation.

causes.name: Mismatched front tires
causes.clues: Different brands, models or wear levels on the front.

causes.name: Alignment off
causes.clues: The pull stays the same no matter which tires are on the front.

you: Check that the front tires match and the pressures are correct.
shop: Swap front tires side to side and road test

result.title: Worn steering or suspension parts are likely letting a wheel shift
result.now: Have the steering and front suspension inspected within the next few days. Drive gently until then.
if: If the steering suddenly feels much looser or the car is hard to keep in its lane, stop driving and have it towed.
If parts are replaced, have an alignment done afterward.
result.why: When tie rods, ball joints or bushings wear, the wheel can move out of position as you drive. That causes a pull that may come and go, along with clunks and uneven tire wear.

causes.name: Worn control arm bushings
causes.clues: A pull that changes between accelerating and braking, and clunks over bumps.

causes.name: Worn tie rod ends
causes.clues: Extra play in the steering wheel and wear on one edge of a front tire.

causes.name: Worn ball joints
causes.clues: Clunking or creaking when turning or going over bumps.

you: Look for uneven wear on the inner or outer edges of the front tires.
Listen for clunks over speed bumps.
shop: Steering and suspension inspection on a lift
Tie rod and ball joint play check

result.title: Wheel alignment is the most likely cause of a steady pull
result.now: Check all four tire pressures first. If they're correct, book an alignment check.
if: If the tires are wearing on one edge, get the alignment done soon to avoid ruining them.
If the pull suddenly gets stronger, or you notice a burning smell or clunking, get it checked within a day or two.
result.why: Alignment is the angle of the wheels. It slowly drifts out with normal wear, bumps and potholes, and when the angles differ side to side the car pulls. Uneven tire wear and an off-center steering wheel often come along with it.

causes.name: Alignment out of spec
causes.clues: The steering wheel is off-center, or the tires wear on one edge.

causes.name: Low or uneven tire pressure
causes.clues: One tire is lower than the others.

causes.name: Worn suspension parts
causes.clues: Clunks over bumps, or the pull comes and goes.

you: Look for wear on the inner or outer edges of the tires.
shop: Alignment check with printed before-and-after readings
